nodes.label: A PCSX2 binding joined with & requires both axes to move at once
nodes.norm_label: a pcsx2 binding joined with & requires both axes to move at once
nodes.summary: The inherited RLeft/RRight entries read `SDL-0/-JoyAxis2 & SDL-0/-JoyAxis3`, i.e. the X and Y axes of the same right stick conjoined. A physical left or right tilt satisfies only one term, so the binding can never fire; splitting each into a single axis restored the direction. Distinct from chunk-rem-085's pcsx2-auto-bind-creates-combined-axis-requirements, which attributes the stray `&` entries to the Atur Tombol Otomatis button rather than to the `&` operator itself.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-games-ps2/2026-09-28 - konfigurasi-umum-stick-playstation-2 [ses_f15d9b788ffeBE5nBLwvpZlgiw].md:L2261] Yang lama butuh 2 axis gerak bareng (`&`), jadi praktis nggak pernah ketrigger.

nodes.label: The SDL database holds two DragonRise entries that disagree on the right-stick Y axis
nodes.norm_label: the sdl database holds two dragonrise entries that disagree on the right-stick y axis
nodes.summary: Matching the stick's GUID against the SDL gamecontroller database is not enough to fix its axes: the database carries variants whose right-stick vertical axis differs (a3 vs a4). The session resolved it by keeping a4 because that was already what RUp/RDown used, and gave the user a manual check. Note the session's GUID 03000000790000000600000000000000 maps rightx:a2/righty:a4, while chunk-rem-085's pcsx2-usb-gamepad-guid-mapping-assigns-rightstick-axes recorded a3/a4 from a different entry, 03000000790000000600000007010000 — the two notes disagree and this one is the narrower claim about the ambiguity.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-games-ps2/2026-09-28 - konfigurasi-umum-stick-playstation-2 [ses_f15d9b788ffeBE5nBLwvpZlgiw].md:L2272] untuk stick ini database SDL beda varian di analog kanan atas/bawah (`a3` vs `a4`). Saya ikut `a4` karena itu yang sudah dipasang di `RUp/RDown` kamu sebelumnya.

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-games-ps2/2026-09-28 - konfigurasi-umum-stick-playstation-2 [ses_f15d9b788ffeBE5nBLwvpZlgiw].md:L2265] GUID SDL `03000000790000000600000000000000` (persis VID/PID stick kamu) di database SDL memang `leftx:a0, lefty:a1, rightx:a2, righty:a4` dengan nomor tombol yang sama persis.

nodes.label: An agent-run timed input-capture window races the human and comes back empty
nodes.norm_label: an agent-run timed input-capture window races the human and comes back empty
nodes.summary: The session opened a 20-second listener on /dev/input/js0, told the user to wiggle the stick, and got an empty capture because the user did not move during the window. The fix recorded in the note is to stop racing: hand the user the command to run themselves so they own the timing. Same shape as the positive-control rule in the machine AGENTS.md.

nodes.label: Rust rodio cues bypass the WebView autoplay policy entirely
nodes.norm_label: rust rodio cues bypass the webview autoplay policy entirely
nodes.summary: The hypothesis under test was that WebKitGTK autoplay policy silenced Snipset's feedback sounds. The investigation found the trigger, clipboard and magic-menu paths the hypothesis targets are Rust + rodio, which never touches WebKit's policy, so the hypothesis is disproven for those paths. Autoplay remains a real, invisible risk for a measured 211 non-gesture webview call sites, but it cannot explain silence on direct button clicks. Related, not identical, to chunk-rem-013/rem-074's webkitgtk-autoplay-policy.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - c5-autoplay-policy-path-split [ses_f1acee208ffeU8QyZUYFQwg8uV].md:L6439] They are pure Rust + rodio, which never touches WebKit's autoplay policy. So the hypothesis is **disproven as the explanation for those paths** — no autoplay policy exists to reject anything there.

nodes.label: Suppressing NotAllowedError with no log makes an autoplay rejection unloggable
nodes.norm_label: suppressing notallowederror with no log makes an autoplay rejection unloggable
nodes.summary: playAudio catches the play() promise and matches NotAllowedError by name — the exact name WebKit uses for an autoplay-policy rejection — then drops it with no console.error, no console.debug, no toast, no IPC report and no metric. The stated debugging consequence: no log pass can ever rule autoplay in or out, so playAudio must be instrumented before the theory can be tested at all.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - c5-autoplay-policy-path-split [ses_f1acee208ffeU8QyZUYFQwg8uV].md:L6510] `NotAllowedError` — which is *precisely* the WebKit autoplay-policy rejection name — is matched and **deliberately dropped with no logging at any level**.

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - c5-autoplay-policy-path-split [ses_f1acee208ffeU8QyZUYFQwg8uV].md:L6520] **if autoplay were the cause, nothing in the logs would ever show it.** A diagnostic pass must therefore instrument `playAudio` before it can rule autoplay in or out.

nodes.label: With no Rust-to-webview audio event bridge, the two audio layers fail independently
nodes.norm_label: with no rust-to-webview audio event bridge, the two audio layers fail independently
nodes.summary: All 30 emitted Rust event names contain no audio/sound/beep/sfx/feedback name, no #[tauri::command] has such a name, and the only audio-matching listen() subscriptions are the speech://audio-level meter. The gap is symmetric: nothing is wired on either side. Because there is no bridge, Rust cannot rescue a webview sound and the webview cannot supplement a Rust sound, which is what produces the reported "some sounds work, others don't" pattern.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - c5-autoplay-policy-path-split [ses_f1acee208ffeU8QyZUYFQwg8uV].md:L6561] **No Rust→webview audio event bridge exists. The gap is symmetric — nothing is wired on either side.**

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - c5-autoplay-policy-path-split [ses_f1acee208ffeU8QyZUYFQwg8uV].md:L6570] because there is no bridge, Rust cannot rescue a webview sound and the webview cannot supplement a Rust sound. Each layer is independently authoritative for its own actions, and there is no fallback.

nodes.label: One audio_feedback preference gates both audio layers and the Settings toggle never notifies Rust
nodes.norm_label: one audio_feedback preference gates both audio layers and the settings toggle never notifies rust
nodes.summary: audio_feedback is read twice, independently — by engine/audio.rs into Rust's AUDIO_ENABLED and by utils/audio.ts into the webview's audioEnabled — and an explicit "false" mutes both. Rust writes AUDIO_ENABLED only once, in init_audio_from_preferences() at startup, while the Settings toggle writes the preference and calls only the local setAudioEnabled. The two layers can therefore disagree for the rest of the session, which is the "some paths silent, others not" signature the report set out to explain.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - c5-autoplay-policy-path-split [ses_f1acee208ffeU8QyZUYFQwg8uV].md:L6578] `audio_feedback` is read independently by `engine/audio.rs:20-24` (Rust, into `AUDIO_ENABLED`) and by `utils/audio.ts:11-21` (webview, into `audioEnabled`). A value of `"false"` mutes everything. Note the Rust side defaults to `true` only when the key is *absent*; an explicit `"false"` mutes.

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - c5-autoplay-policy-path-split [ses_f1acee208ffeU8QyZUYFQwg8uV].md:L6580] `AUDIO_ENABLED` is written **only** in `init_audio_from_preferences()` (`engine/audio.rs:24`), called once at startup (`setup/init.rs:144`). The Settings toggle writes the preference and calls the local `setAudioEnabled` (`useSettingsPanel.ts:312-321`) but **never notifies Rust**.

nodes.label: Cargo resolver 2 does not unify features requested by a non-applicable target table
nodes.norm_label: cargo resolver 2 does not unify features requested by a non-applicable target table
nodes.summary: The workspace sets resolver = "2" and apps/desktop/src-tauri declares no package.resolver, so resolver 2 governs. Resolver 2 does not unify features requested by a target table that does not apply to the build target, so a feature added to the linux-only dependencies table applies on Linux only. Verified against the workspace manifest lines quoted in the note.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - r2-arboard-feature-claim [ses_f1cff6780ffeiHHmQREM2XoGJQ].md:L3492] Resolver 2 does not unify features requested by a non-applicable target table → the Linux-scoped request applies on Linux only.

nodes.label: Two mutually exclusive target tables can never union, so they prove nothing about feature union
nodes.norm_label: two mutually exclusive target tables can never union, so they prove nothing about feature union
nodes.summary: The plan cited rodio declared once under not(windows) and once under windows as evidence the manifest already relies on overlapping target tables. Those two cfg sets are mutually exclusive, so the entries can never apply together and the precedent is worthless. The genuine precedent in the same manifest is mac_address, whose not(android) and windows tables both apply on Windows.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - r2-arboard-feature-claim [ses_f1cff6780ffeiHHmQREM2XoGJQ].md:L3493] `rodio` at `:114` (`not(windows)`) and `:128` (`windows`) are mutually exclusive, so those two entries can never union and prove nothing about feature union.

nodes.label: arboard's Wayland backend stays selected on a compositor lacking zwlr_data_control_manager_v1
nodes.norm_label: arboard's wayland backend stays selected on a compositor lacking zwlr_data_control_manager_v1
nodes.summary: The plan claimed arboard logs a warning and falls back to X11 when the compositor lacks zwlr_data_control_manager_v1. The reviewer found the opposite: wayland.rs returns Ok for every Ok value from is_primary_selection_supported ("We don't care if the primary clipboard is supported"), so the X11 fallback warning never fires, the backend stays Wayland, and reads fail per-operation with Error::ContentNotAvailable or Error::Unknown. Corrected in the note as a distinct outcome from an X11 session, to be confirmed live rather than assumed. wl-clipboard-rs is not vendored, so the inner branch could not be proven from local source.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - r2-arboard-feature-claim [ses_f1cff6780ffeiHHmQREM2XoGJQ].md:L3495] (c) compositor without `zwlr_data_control_manager_v1` → the plan is WRONG: `wayland.rs:97-105` returns `Ok(_) => Ok(Self {})` (comment: "We don't care if the primary clipboard is supported"), so the mod.rs:138-142 X11 fallback warning does NOT fire and the backend stays Wayland, failing per-operation

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - r2-arboard-feature-claim [ses_f1cff6780ffeiHHmQREM2XoGJQ].md:L3506] arboard's wayland backend still initialises successfully (arboard wayland.rs:99-104 returns Ok for every Ok value from is_primary_selection_supported), so no X11 fallback warning is logged and reads fail per-operation with Error::ContentNotAvailable or Error::Unknown.

nodes.label: ashpd pulls zbus, not wayland-client
nodes.summary: The plan reasoned about a duplicate wayland-client major "beside the copy ashpd already pulls". ashpd 0.13.13 pulls only enumflags2, futures-util, getrandom, serde, tokio and zbus. The wayland-client already in the lock arrives through libwayshot-xcap (via xcap), so the plan's premise about where the existing copy comes from is false.
